newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close lower after setting new high in Dec.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close lower after setting new high in Dec.

text.p: CME hog futures posted a new contract high in December before profit taking pressured the market and prices finished lower. Lean contracts paced the loss on projections of increased hog numbers later and posted new contract lows in distant October to April.

December posted a new contract high of 59.625 cent and then retreated to close 0.175 lower at 59.200 cents. Lean contracts fell for losses of 0.750 to 1.025 cents by the close with farthest months setting new lows.
Fund buying and commercial support limited the setback in December, traders said.

Cash hog and pork product markets have been holding stronger than expected and this kept that month supported. Profit taking in February and April weighed on those months, especially after the recent runup in values and posting of a new high in February on Monday, they said.
Deferred months showed added pressure from ideas hog numbers will be much larger later in 1997. Hogs kept back for breeding now will come to market as early as next summer, traders said.
"Those (back) months are showing expectations for the next pig crop report," one trader said.
In hog options, deep in-the-money calls were offered in December on the early rally and there was mostly expiration type trade later, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures followed the lead of live hogs early but turned weaker late as profit taking increased and touched off some sell stops. The market appeared due for a correction after the recent sharp runup in values, especially when it failed to fill a gap in the charts, traders said.
Bellies closed 1.600 to 0.050 cent lower with February off 1.400 at 79.975 cents. Further losses were expected Wednesday following the weekly CME out-of-town report.
The CME reported a net in-movement last week of 3,313 million lbs, well above the range of early estimates of unchanged to in 1.5 million lbs.

Impact could be limited by the downward revised hog slaughter rate. Tuesday's USDA estimated hog slaughter was near the low end of analyst expectations and Monday's estimated kill was revised downward.

"Hog slaughter was light and Monday's revised downward and I think that will support the bellies much more than the out-of-town will hurt the bellies," said Dennis Smith, broker with LIT division of First Options.
